fullText:
This is a pretty cool idea:

Let your agent simulate each potential action before picking the best one.

The model is PAN 2, a world model from the Institute of Foundation Models (IFM). They call this "simulative reasoning".

The attached video shows an example with a surfer: same wave, three different moments to pop up. PAN 2 plays out all three, and only one of them catches the wave, so that’s the one he goes with.

The model uses Generative Latent Prediction (GLP), and here is how it works:

• In: the current scene plus an action, with how long to simulate

• Out: what happens next, as a video you can check

There are two reasoning parts:

1. Conceptual reasoning: The LLM is the backbone here. It reasons about what happens next.

2. Perceptual reasoning: A 29B LDM fills in what it looks like.

This is all open under Apache 2.0!

They provided the weights, training code, and inference code, so you can run it and build on it yourself.

fullText:
Impressive paper from Robbyant on physical AI.

(bookmark it)

Robot hands use a range of tactile sensors, and a model trained on one sensor can struggle to transfer to another.

That's a big challenge in robotics right now.

LingBot-Touch is a foundation model to address this challenge. It was pretrained on 4,983 hours of real touch data.

They tested it on the XHand1, a robot hand whose sensor the model never saw. The model stayed frozen. Only a small add-on was trained to find where the fingertip is pressed.

On XHand1, the average contact-center error was 0.16 mm with LingBot-Touch versus 5.89 mm with FTP-1 using an XHand1-specific adapter. That's about a 97% reduction in error.

It transfers because every sensor maps to the same virtual fingertip. Training also varies touch-point density and placement, so the model can't memorize one sensor.

Better touch also makes robots better at tasks. Across six real-world XHand1 tasks, LingBot-VLA averaged 57.21% success both without tactile input and with raw tactile input, rising to 75.04% with LingBot-Touch features.

In simulated RL, it scored highest on all twelve tasks. Plate spinning went from 0.5% to 97.4%.

Has anyone seen a frozen touch model transfer to a new sensor like this?

fullText:
蚂蚁刚开源了一个触觉基础模型：LingBot-Touch，让机器人不仅能看得见，还能感知“手感”

这种触觉经验能跨传感器、跨灵巧手、跨模型、跨任务复用

这个方向值得关注，因为机器人在真实世界中做精细操作，光靠视觉是远远不够的，需要指尖的接触和受力反馈

还有一个迁移问题

LingBot-Touch的做法是，把触觉感知从特定硬件中抽象出来，训练成可复用的基础模型能力

基于近5000小时真实触觉数据预训练，覆盖磁触觉、视触觉和压阻式三类传感原理

并给不同传感器设置专用编码入口，再把不同布局的触点映射到统一的指尖坐标空间，通过共享模型学习接触位置、受力及其随时间的变化，最终输出统一的触觉Token

这样，不同传感器采集的数据可以共同参与预训练，不同灵巧手和动作模型也能复用学到的触觉表征

相当于给机器人建立了一套跨硬件的通用触觉表征

实验效果，平均任务成功率比无触觉基线提高了14-26个百分点

过去，不同机器人往往需要分别采集触觉数据、适配传感器、训练模型

现在不用每换一套灵巧手、增加一种传感器，就从头积累触觉数据、重新学习接触感知能力了

现在虽然不用考 LeetCode 了，但要考 AI Coding 了，并不见得容易些，还更玄学。

以下内容来自 Reddit 的帖子

-------

致所有觉得 AI 面试很好的人：那就祝你好运吧 :) 彭博社面试经历 [伦敦/法兰克福]

刚刚面完彭博社的第二轮 AI 代码库 (codebase) 面试。

考察的是 Python 的 Django 框架，而我对此一无所知。而且整个代码库非常庞大。

他们在前 30 分钟都在进行行为面试 (behavioral interview) ，所以留给你写代码的时间基本上就只剩 30 分钟了。

关于 AI 工具的使用边界非常模糊。你根本不知道面试官到底允许你用多大程度的 AI，他们也不会明确说出自己的期望。我使用了 planning mode 和 ask mode，一个功能接一个功能地推进，虽然通过了几个测试用例，但最后还是被拒了。

用 AI 辅助时需要阅读大量的生成内容，如果还要同时兼顾和面试官沟通交流，这几乎是不可能完成的任务。

以前刷 LeetCode  的时候，至少题目是明确的，你只需要想办法解题就行，哪怕卡住了也可以头脑风暴各种思路。但在这种愚蠢的 AI 面试里，光是为了搞懂那个庞大的代码库、弄清楚问题到底出在哪里，就已经耗掉了一半的时间。

致那些之前还在庆祝“LeetCode 时代终结”的人：祝你们好运吧。现在的面试只会难得多。

哦对了，千万别动“靠一句提示词让 AI 一次性秒杀整道题 (one-shotting)”的念头，否则你照样会被拒（我朋友就遇到了这种情况）。

不管怎么说，AI 面试简直就是天大的扯淡，你永远不可能找到一套稳定、通用的方法去应对这种面试。

online travel has always been half broken. 

You book a flight in one place, a hotel in another, and activities in a third.

And you watch YouTube videos for travel ideas. 

Agentic AI may finally solve this disjointed process. 

Note: I have a full podcast episode on this. Link below.

Point 1: GenAI's real superpower is coordination.
 Traditional Platforms connect buyers and sellers only when merchants enters data in one standard format.

Point 2: Travel is where platform business models break.
 Travelers bounce between https://t.co/tqigVxjteP, airlines, Viator and videos as human middleware.

Point 3: Agentic AI becomes the connective tissue.

GenAI enables coordination between different platforms and data types. 

just like humans. 

***Takeaways for Managers:

Takeaway 1: Map one workflow and assign each step to rules, analytics, generative AI or agents.

See McKinsey graphic. 

I go deeper on this in Episode 270 of The Tech Strategy Podcast.
 https://t.co/UBQINXXS6x

QUESTION: Who wins travel bookings in an agent world, OTAs or hotels? Why?

#AgenticAI #Ecommerce #Travel #Podcast
